rule.name: Remove spaces before certain punctuation, typically . , : ; ? !
rule.description: No space is placed before certain punctuation marks

rule.name: Convert two periods (..) in parenthesis by ellipsis (…)
rule.description: Two consecutive dots in parentheses or brackets most likely indicate an error and should be replaced with an ellipsis

rule.name: Convert all nonbreaking hyphens to regular hyphens
rule.description: Convert all nonbreaking hyphens to regular hyphens and eventually add them later by specific rule

rule.name: Two hyphens to en-dash
rule.description: Two hyphens to en-dash

rule.name: Convert figure dash to dash between letters
rule.description: Converts figure dash U+2012 into standard dash

rule.name: Remove zero-width characters (U+200B–200D)
rule.description: Remove zero-width spaces, zero-width non-joiner and zero-width joiner to make GREP-based search and replace operations more effective

rule.name: Em-dash to en-dash
rule.description: Em-dash to en-dash

rule.name: Three or four periods to ellipsis (U+2026)
rule.description: Three or four periods to ellipsis

rule.name: Remove all soft hyphens (U+00AD)
rule.description: Remove all soft hyphens (SHY) to make GREP-based search and replace operations more effective

rule.name: Replace two single open quotes ‚ ‚ with one double opening quotation mark „ (correct form of quotation marks to be modified in next step)
rule.description: Replace two commas {U+002C} or two low-9 quotation mark (U+201A) double low-9 quotation mark (U+201E)

rule.name: Delete space between quotation marks (hairspace could be added consistently in the next step if required)
rule.description: If primary and secondary quotation marks appear consecutively in the text, no spaces are inserted between them (unless this is a deliberate typographical choice)

rule.name: Replace two single quotes ‹ ‹ with one double quotation mark « (correct form of quotation marks to be modified in next step)
rule.description: Replace two single left-pointing angle quotation ‹‹ (U+2039) to left-pointing double angle quotation « (U+00AB)

example.before: ‹‹word word‹‹ (The change may not be visible, change font style to Typofix EU Special to see the difference)
example.after: «word word« (The change may not be visible, change font style to Typofix EU Special to see the difference)

rule.name: Replace two single quotes › › with one double quotation mark » (correct form of quotation marks to be modified in next step)
rule.description: Replace two single right-pointing angle quotation ›› (U+203A) to left-pointing double angle quotation » (U+00BB)

example.before: ››word word›› (The change may not be visible, change font style to Typofix EU Special to see the difference)
example.after: »word word» (The change may not be visible, change font style to Typofix EU Special to see the difference)

rule.name: Convert comma to baseline single quote ‚ if used inappropriately
rule.description: Convert comma to baseline single quote ‚

example.before: My ,friend‘ (The change may not be visible, change font style to Typofix EU Special to see the difference)
example.after: My ‚friend‘ (The change may not be visible, change font style to Typofix EU Special to see the difference)

rule.name: Replace multiple tabs by single tab
rule.description: Multiple tabs are likely a mistake in the text, although they may be part of a legacy table format. In most cases, it is safe to replace them with a single tab (or eventually replace them with a space, or remove them entirely)

category.name: Spaces
Run first – remove extra or double spaces, convert all spaces to standard space (prefs)

rule.name: Remove all kinds of spaces (horizontal and vertical) at the end of the story
rule.description: Removing all vertical and horizontal spaces at the end of a thread.

category.name: Spaces
Run first – remove extra or double spaces, convert all spaces to standard space (prefs)

example.before: This is the end of story. This is the end of story.
example.after: This is the end of story. This is the end of story.

rule.name: Remove spaces adjacent to a tab
rule.description: Spaces next to tabs serve no purpose in the text and should be deleted

category.name: Spaces
Run first – remove extra or double spaces, convert all spaces to standard space (prefs)

example.before: text ↦ text text↦ text text ↦text text ↦

rule.name: Ratio / map scale without spaces around colon
rule.description: Remove spaces around colon in ratios (1:100)

rule.name: Delete an extra space at the end of a paragraph
rule.description: A space at the end of a paragraph or article is unnecessary and should be deleted

rule.name: Delete an extra space at the beginning of a paragraph
rule.description: There should be no space at the beginning of a paragraph; any paragraph indentation can be adjusted by setting the paragraph parameters in the application

rule.name: Keep short dates together using nonbreaking spaces (12. 09. 1974)
rule.description: The short date format is written with non-breaking spaces to prevent the expression from being split at the end of a line

rule.name: Connect v. with surname
rule.description: Replace space by nonbreaking spaces between v. (= von) and surname

rule.description: An initial or group of initials is connected to the name with an non-breaking space so that they do not appear at the end of a line

rule.name: Connect initials using nonbreaking space (J. F. or J. R. R.)
rule.description: A space is typically written between initials; in some languages, you can choose the width of this space in the preferences.

example.before: J. F. Kennedy J. R. R. Tolkien
example.after: J. F. Kennedy J. R. R. Tolkien

rule.name: Nonbreaking spaces in two-part abbreviations
rule.description: In established abbreviations consisting of two parts – such as names of institutions or media outlets – a non-breaking space is used to prevent them from being split at the end of a line

example.before: France 24 Al Jazeera Teil 6 (German) TV 2 (Danish) ČT 1 (Czech) AV ČR (Czech) III Rzesza (Polish) ÚS SR (Slovak) TVR 2 (Romanian) HRT 2 (Croatian)
example.after: France 24 Al Jazeera Teil 6 (German) TV 2 (Danish) ČT 1 (Czech) AV ČR (Czech) III Rzesza (Polish) ÚS SR (Slovak) TVR 2 (Romanian) HRT 2 (Croatian)

rule.name: Keep Pantone numbers with suffixes
rule.description: Pantone number code should not be separated from suffix C or U

rule.name: Connect town name with a district number (Praha 1)
rule.description: In some countries, city districts are numbered using Arabic numbers, these elements should be joined with a non-breaking space so they do not split at the end of a line

example.before: Praha 10 (Czech, Slovak) Ostrava 2 (Czech) Plzeň 3 (Czech) Bratislava 1 (Czech, Slovak) Dublin 18 or Dublin 6W (English, Irish) Ní féidir liom a bheith gan Bhaile Átha Cliath 2. (Irish)
example.after: Praha 10 (Czech, Slovak) Ostrava 2 (Czech) Plzeň 3 (Czech) Bratislava 1 (Czech, Slovak) Dublin 18 or Dublin 6W (English, Irish) Ní féidir liom a bheith gan Bhaile Átha Cliath 2. (Irish)

rule.name: Connect town name with a district Roman number (Liberec IV)
rule.description: In some countries, city districts are numbered using Roman numerals, these elements should be joined with a non-breaking space so they do not split at the end of a line

example.before: Pardubice VII (Czech, Slovak) Pardubice I-Staré Město (Czech, Slovak) Pardubice I – Staré Město (Czech Academic)
example.after: Pardubice VII (Czech, Slovak) Pardubice I-Staré Město (Czech Traditional, Slovak) Pardubice I – Staré Město (Czech Academic)

rule.name: Nonbreaking space between single-word abbreviations and numbers (Nr. 20)
rule.description: There should be a non-breaking space between the abbreviation and the number to prevent the expression from being split at the end of the line

example.before: IQ 151 (many languages) ID 48006584 (all languages) tel. 244 (many languages)
example.after: IQ 151 (many languages) ID 48006584 (all languages) tel. 244 (many languages)

rule.name: Nonbreaking space between abbreviations and words (e.g. Doe)
rule.description: There should be a non-breaking space between the abbreviation and the following word so that the abbreviation does not end up at the end of the line

rule.name: Nonbreaking space in two-part abbreviations of academic degrees with periods
rule.description: Replaces normal space in abbreviations like "Mgr. Art." by nonbreaking space and adds a space after the last period if missing

example.before: Den Vortrag hielt o. Prof. Dr. Hans Müller. o.Prof. (German)
example.after: Den Vortrag hielt o. Prof. Dr. Hans Müller. o. Prof. (German)

rule.name: Non-breaking Space in Biblical Book Abbreviations (Tim, 2 Tim etc.)
rule.description: The numbered abbreviations of the books of the Bible should include a non-breaking space to prevent the term from being split at the end

rule.name: Non-breaking space in Bible verse reference
rule.description: Bible book, chapter and verse should be connected by non-breaking space so as to avoid splitting the expression at the end of the line

example.before: 1 Co 15,26 (French, Spanish) 1 Cor 15,26 (English, Italian, Romanian) 1 Kor. 15:26 (Dutch)
example.after: 1 Co 15,26 (French, Spanish) 1 Cor 15,26 (English, Italian, Romanian) 1 Kor. 15:26 (Dutch)

rule.name: Connect numbers up to four digits before closing parenthesis with the last word (final value 11)
rule.description: A number in parentheses should not start the next line, so it is joined to the preceding word with a non-breaking space

rule.name: Nonbreaking space after abbreviations marking birth or death before the date
rule.description: Abbreviations to mark birth or death before the date are separated by a nonbreaking space

rule.name: Thin spaces in three-part abbreviations with periods
rule.description: Replaces normal spaces in abbreviations like s. r. o. by thin spaces

rule.name: Correct spaces and punctuation in Czech and Slovak abbreviation spol. s r. o.
rule.description: Replaces normal spaces in Czech and Slovak abbreviation spol. s r. o.

example.before: spol. s r. o. spol.s r.o.
example.after: spol. s r. o. spol. s r. o.

rule.name: Narrow spaces in two-part abbreviations with periods
rule.description: Replaces normal spaces in abbreviations like u. Ä. by narrow spaces

example.before: Für die Reparatur brauchen wir Schrauben, Dübel u. Ä.
example.after: Für die Reparatur brauchen wir Schrauben, Dübel u. Ä.

rule.name: Remove spaces before ellipsis – preferences
rule.description: Remove space before ellipsis if preceded by alphabetic characters (optional setting in preferences)

rule.name: Add missing spaces after closing parenthesis or brackets
rule.description: Add missing spaces after closing parenthesis or brackets

rule.name: Replace standard spaces by nonbreaking spaces in numbers
rule.description: Replace standard spaces by nonbreaking spaces (or alternative separators) in numbers. Works only with numbers separated by a regular space into groups of three digits (1 000 000)

rule.name: Use periods for thousand separators instead of spaces
rule.description: Replace spaces by periods in numbers. Works only with numbers separated by a space into groups of three digits (1.000.000)

example.before: This feature must be turned on in preferences 1 000 000 000 000 000 1 000 +420 775 223 197 (to be fixed) 3,141592 (no change) 1974 (no change)
example.after: This feature must be turned on in preferences 1.000.000.000.000.000 1.000,99 +420 775 223 197 (to be fixed) 3,141592 (no change) 1974 (no change)

rule.name: Replace space by nonbreaking space between ordinal number marked with period and following word
rule.description: Replace space by nonbreaking space between ordinal number marked with period and following word (1. místo)

rule.name: Change any hyphen or dash preceding numbers to minus sign (U+2212) From -2 to −2
rule.description: Hyphens or dashes preceding numbers that are at the beginning of a paragraph, after an opening parenthesis, brackets, braces, or preceded by a space.

rule.name: Connect capitalised names with Roman numerals (useful for popes, emperors – Charles IV etc.)
rule.description: The name is joined to the Roman numeral with a non-breaking space to prevent the expression from being split at the end of a line

example.before: Charles IV Johannes Paul II Karl IV Kehä III
example.after: Charles IV Johannes Paul II Karl IV Kehä III

rule.name: Replace space by nonbreaking space between Roman ordinal number marked by period and following word
rule.description: Keep Roman ordinal number marked by period and following word (III. epizoda)

example.before: III. díl (Czech) XVIII.storočie (Slovak) III. zvezek (Slovenian) XXXI. kötet (Hungarian) XI. freundschaftliche Begegnung III.izdanje (Croatian)
example.after: III. díl (Czech) XVIII. storočie (Slovak) III. zvezek (Slovenian) XXXI. kötet (Hungarian) XI. freundschaftliche Begegnung III. izdanje (Croatian)

rule.name: Nonbreaking space between abbreviations and Roman numbers (Nr. XVI)
rule.description: There should be a non-breaking space between the abbreviation and the number to prevent the expression from being split at the end of the line

rule.name: Remove duplicate redundant punctuation before closing parenthesis
rule.description: Commas and semicolons are not repeated and are only placed after parentheses

example.before: Type punctuation (comma,), then save the file. (any language)
example.after: Type punctuation (comma), then save the file. (any language)

rule.name: Add period after certain abbreviations if missing
rule.description: Add period after certain abbreviations if missing (et al > et al.)

rule.name: Remove Spanish inverted punctuation in languages other than Spanish
rule.description: Inverted punctuation (¡ ¿ ⸘) is only used at the start of a sentence in Spanish; therefore, it must be removed in other languages.

example.before: ¿Къде са тоалетните? ¡Λοιπόν, αυτό! ⸘Wie ist das möglich‽ ¿¡⸘
example.after: Къде са тоалетните? Λοιπόν, αυτό! Wie ist das möglich‽ [should be empty]

rule.name: Comma in Bible verse reference 1 Kor 3,18 or Mt 12,43–44
rule.description: For Bible references, the chapter and verse numbers are separated by a comma

example.before: Der Vers 1 Kor 15:26 spricht vom letzten Feind. 1 Kor 15:26 (Ps 23:1–3)
example.after: Der Vers 1 Kor 15,26 spricht vom letzten Feind. 1 Kor 15,26 (Ps 23,1–3)

rule.name: Replaces two periods by a single period
rule.description: A second period is not repeated at the end of a sentence or phrase. (However, it is possible that the author intended an ellipsis …)

example.before: three dots… (not affected) two dots.. two (..) dots two.. dots τρείς τελείες… (not affected) δύο τελείες.. δύο (..) τελείες δύο.. τελείες
example.after: three dots… (not affected) two dots. two (.) dots two. dots τρείς τελείες… (not affected) δύο τελείες. δύο (.) τελείες δύο. τελείες

rule.name: Wrong apostrophe to the correct form at the end of a word
rule.description: A proper apostrophe has the specific shape of a small number 9 or a line that tapers downward and slopes to the right

example.before: test ’s (no change) test ‘s’ (quotation marks may change to a version defined in preferences
example.after: test ’s (no change) test ‘s’ (quotation marks may change to a version defined in preferences)

rule.name: Wrong apostrophe to the correct form ’ (U+2019) inside expressions
rule.description: A proper apostrophe has the specific shape of a small number 9 or a line that tapers downward and slopes to the right

example.before: Kelly's d‘Artagnan L‘Humanité He`ll Pierre´em Curie They‘ve 80‘erne test ’s (no change) test ‘s’ (quotation marks may change to a version defined in preferences
example.after: Kelly’s d’Artagnan L’Humanité He’ll Pierre’em Curie They’ve 80’erne test ’s (no change) test ‘s’ (quotation marks may change to a version defined in preferences

rule.name: Upside down apostrophe to correct form ’ in French expressions
rule.description: The correct form of the apostrophe resembles either a small 9 or a comma that narrows towards the bottom

rule.name: Fix spelling of rock ’n’ roll
rule.description: The rock ’n’ roll is writen with spaces and apostrophes on both sides of the letter “n”

example.after: rock ’n’ roll rock ’n’ roll rock ’n’ roll

rule.name: Secondary quotation marks ‚x‘
rule.description: Replace the secondary quotation marks in the text with the ‚x‘ style

rule.name: Primary quotation marks „ “
rule.description: Use the appropriate quotation marks for the selected language; the default is these „quotation“ marks, but you can change them in the settings

rule.name: Change quotation marks inside quotation marks from primary to secondary (“Word: ‘Word’!”)
rule.description: Change quotation marks inside quotation marks from primary to secondary (“Word: ‘Word’!”)

example.before: „Double „quotation“ test.“ (Czech, German, Slovak…) „Double „quotation” test.” (Hungarian, Polish…) „Double „quotation” test.” (Croatian…) „Double „quotation” test.” (Dutch…) «Double «quotation» test.» (Italian, Spanish, Portuguese, Greek…) “Double “quotation” test.” (US English, Irish) ‘Double ‘quotation’ test.’ (UK English) ”Double ”quotation” test.” (Finnish – does not work yet) »Double »quotation« test.« (Slovenian)
example.after: „Double ‚quotation‘ test.“ (Croatian, Czech, German, Slovak…) „Double »quotation« test.” (Hungarian, Polish…) „Double ‘quotation’ test.” (Croatian…) „Double ‚quotation’ test.” (Dutch…) «Double “quotation” test.» (Italian, Spanish, Portuguese, Greek…) “Double ‘quotation’ test.” (US English, Irish) ‘Double “quotation” test.’ (UK English) ”Double ’quotation’ test.” (Finnish – does not work yet) »Double ›quotation‹ test.« (Slovenian)

rule.name: En-dash without spaces instead of a hyphen between cardinal numbers (range)
rule.description: En-dash without spaces instead of a hyphen with or without spaces between cardinal numbers (ie. 1–2)

rule.name: The correct form of born in year (1974–)
rule.description: The correct form of born in year (1974–) with endash between parenthesis

rule.name: Hyphens instead of dashes between four number groups (ISBN)
rule.description: Hyphens instead of dashes between four number groups (ISBN) incl. control number X

rule.name: Change hyphen to a dash at the beginning of a paragraph
rule.description: Change hyphen to a dash followed by a fixed width space at the beginning of a paragraph (- hello > – hello) to create dialogs or lists

rule.name: Endash without spaces instead of a hyphen between a span of week days (ie. mo–fr)
rule.description: The days of the week are written with an en-dash, without spaces on either side

example.before: pondělí - pátek (Czech) Mo – Fr (English) poniedziałek-piątek (Polish) пн-пт (Bulgarian) lun. – ven. (French) Fr-So (German) Man - Søn (Danish) H-Sze (Hungarian) joi – sâm. (Romanian) E - R (Estonian) Pr - Sv (Latvian) Pr—Pn (Lithuanian) lun. - mar. (Spanish)
example.after: pondělí–pátek (Czech) Mo–Fr (English) poniedziałek–piątek (Polish) пн–пт (Bulgarian) lun.–ven. (French) Fr–So (German) Man–Søn (Danish) H–Sze (Hungarian) joi–sâm. (Romanian) E–R (Estonian) Pr–Sv (Latvian) Pr–Pn (Lithuanian) lun.–mar. (Spanish)

rule.name: Convert all hyphens in the musical key string to non-breaking hyphens
rule.description: Musical Keys: Ces-dur Ges-dur Des-dur fis-moll cis-moll gis-moll dis-moll ais-moll etc.

example.before: Ces-dur (Czech, Slovak, German, Polish) fis-moll (Czech, Slovak, German, Polish) G-dur (Czech, Slovak, German, Polish) F majeur of bes mineur (Dutch) a–mol (Danish) g-dur (no change) C-moll (no change) As - duur – La-bemoll mažoor (Estonian) G-dúr (Hungarian)
example.after: Ces‑dur (Czech, Slovak, German, Polish) fis‑moll (Czech, Slovak, German, Polish) G‑dur (Czech, Slovak, German, Polish) F-majeur of bes-mineur (Dutch) a‑mol (Danish) g‑dur (no change) C‑moll (no change) As‑duur – La-bemoll mažoor (Estonian) G‑dúr (Hungarian)

rule.name: En-dash without spaces instead of a hyphen between a span of months (January–March)
rule.description: A range of months is written with an en-dash and no spaces on either side

example.before: November — December (English, Hungarian, Swedish, Danish, Dutch) leden - květen (Czech) January – March (English) marts-juni (Danish) lokakuu - marraskuu (Finnish) oktoober – november (Estonian) enero — marzo de 2002 (Spanish) octombrie - noiembrie (Romanian) oktobris - novembris (Latvian) spalis -lapkritis (Lithuanian) outubro- novembro (Portuguese) Styczeń-grudzień (Polish) Dúnta Eanáir-Feabhra (Irish)
example.after: November–December (English, Hungarian, Swedish, Danish, Dutch) leden–květen (Czech) January–March (English) marts–juni (Danish) lokakuu–marraskuu (Finnish) oktoober–november (Estonian) enero–marzo de 2002 (Spanish) octombrie–noiembrie (Romanian) oktobris–novembris (Latvian) spalis–lapkritis (Lithuanian) outubro–novembro (Portuguese) Styczeń–grudzień (Polish) Dúnta Eanáir–Feabhra (Irish)

rule.name: Hyphens instead of dashes between two number groups (ISSN)
rule.description: Nonbreaking hyphens instead of dashes between two number groups (ISSN and ISMN)

example.before: ISSN 2000–2024 ISSN: 1903 - 0661 2000–2024 (no change in most languages) 2000–2024 (Slovak)
example.after: ISSN 2000‑2024 ISSN: 1903‑0661 2000–2024 (no change in most languages) 2000 – 2024 (Slovak)

rule.name: Hyphens instead of dashes between five number groups (ISBN)
rule.description: Hyphens instead of dashes between five number groups (ISBN) incl. control number X

rule.name: Hyphens instead of dashes between three number groups (ISBN)
rule.description: Nonbreaking hyphens instead of dashes between three number groups (ISBN) incl. control number X

rule.name: En-dash without spaces instead of a hyphen between Roman numbers (IV–XIII)
rule.description: The range of Roman numerals is written with a hyphen and no spaces

example.before: MDCXXIV - MCDXXXIX I – III IV-VIII MDCXLIX—MDCCLIX

rule.name: Connect two words with hyphen (geographical locations)
rule.description: Use a hyphen in two-word compounds (geographical locations like Baden-Württemberg)

example.before: Frýdek - Místek (Czech) Frýdku–Místku (Czech) Rakousko–Uhersko (Czech) Edam—Volendam (Dutch) Mandri - Eesti (Estonian) Baden - Württemberg (German) Bielsko -Biała (Polish) Rakúsko – Uhorsko (Slovak) Boldești - Scăeni (Romanian) Rușii–Munți (Romanian) Royaume - Uni (French)
example.after: Frýdek-Místek (Czech) Frýdku-Místku (Czech) Rakousko-Uhersko (Czech) Edam-Volendam (Dutch) Mandri-Eesti (Estonian) Tikka-Mannila (Finnish) Baden-Württemberg (German) Bielsko-Biała (Polish) Rakúsko-Uhorsko (Slovak) Boldești-Scăeni (Romanian) Rușii-Munți (Romanian) Royaume-Uni (French)

rule.name: Connect two words with hyphen (know-how)
rule.description: A hyphen is used in compound words, and it is always written without spaces

example.before: S - Bahn know–how e – mail Hewlett - Packard T–Mobile Harley – Davidson Skłodowska - Curie Curie - Skłodowská (Czech, Slovak) krížom–krážom (Slovak) co - founder (English) πέρα–δώθε (Greek)
example.after: S-Bahn know-how e-mail Hewlett-Packard T-Mobile Harley-Davidson Curie-Skłodowská (Czech, Slovak) Skłodowska-Curie (Polish) krížom-krážom (Slovak) co-founder (English) πέρα-δώθε (Greek)

rule.name: Two hyphens to en-dash at the beginning of a paragraph
rule.description: Two hyphens at the beginning of a paragraph should be replaced with a proper dash. This indicates a list or dialogue and is therefore separated by a fixed-width non-breaking space

rule.name: Hyphen to en-dash preceded by a nonbreaking space
rule.description: Hyphen to parenthetical en-dash preceded by a nonbreaking space to keep dashes at the end of the line (includes possible comma after dash)

rule.name: En-dash without spaces instead of a hyphen between decades (1980s–1990s)
rule.description: The range of decades is written with an en-dash, without a space

rule.name: Remove extra spaces before closing quotation marks
rule.description: Expressions in quotation marks are always written without spaces before the closing quotation marks

rule.description: Add space after closing quotation marks if missing

rule.name: Always use nonbreaking space between value and percent symbol (20 %)
rule.description: Always use nonbreaking space between value and % symbol

rule.description: Insert narrow space after asterisk before year or date to express born in (* 1974)

rule.name: Remove space between word and symbol (typically trade mark ™ and registered ®)
rule.description: Symbols following words (™, ® etc.) are written directly without a space

rule.name: Alert: two capital letters at the beginning of a word
rule.description: Two capital letters are not written consecutively at the beginning of a sentence or certain words. However, exceptions may be made for company names, product names, service names, or intentional neologisms.

example.before: EXample of the PRoblem. (Incorrect English) Example of the Problem. (Correct English)

rule.name: Alert: two consecutive identical parentheses or brackets
rule.description: Two identical parentheses in a row are usually incorrect; one of them may be superfluous. However, they may be secondary parentheses, which should have a different form. Or perhaps everything is fine in this particular context.

rule.name: Alert: sentence probably starts with lowercase letter
rule.description: The beginning of a sentence should start with a capital letter. However, it is possible that in a given context, the use of a lowercase letter is correct.

example.before: (Hello.) new sentence. (Incorrect English) (Hello.) New sentence. (Correct English) “Hi!” my name is Judy. (Incorrect English) “Hi!” My name is Judy. (Correct English) Filip, Linda atd. jsou kamarádi. (Correct Czech)

rule.name: Alert: capital letter after ordinal Arabic or Roman number
rule.description: The ordinal number marked with a period is likely followed by a sentence, so the word should not begin with a lowercase letter. However, it is possible that this is a different situation where a capital letter is correct.

example.before: Karel IV. Je král. (Incorrect Czech) Karel IV. je král. (Correct Czech)

rule.name: Alert: multiple meanings of “I.”
rule.description: The expression “I.” can refer to the Roman ordinal number one, or an abbreviation of a proper name. Based on the context, this term should be connected to the preceding or following word with a non-breaking space.

example.before: Karel I. je král. (incorrect Czech) Karel I. je král. (correct Czech) Karel I. Nováka nepoznal. (incorrect Czech) Karel I. Nováka nepoznal. (correct Czech)

rule.name: Alert: a word followed by hyphen
rule.description: A word followed by hyphen could be intentional (Ein- oder Zweizimmerwohnung) or the hyphen could represent dash or hyphen with or without spaces depending on context and language.

example.before: Ein – oder Zweizimmerwohnung (German incorrect) Ein- oder Zweizimmerwohnung (German correct) Nosotros —o tú-. (Spanish incorrect) Nosotros —o tú—. (Spanish correct) Říkáš- li pravdu… (Czech incorrect) Říkáš‑li pravdu… (Czech) budynki jedno- i dwupiętrowe (Polish correct) motywy staro- i nowotestamentowe (Polish correct) kroje jedno- lub dwuelementowe (Polish correct) układy jedno- i wielopoziomowe (Polish correct) reakcje endo- lub egzotermiczne (Polish correct) mono- i poligamia makro- i mikroekonomia elektro- i gazowe

rule.name: Alert: It is possible that this is an incorrectly typed expression “à la”
rule.description: It is possible that this is an incorrectly typed expression “à la” meaning “in the style of”

rule.name: Alert: Two initials connected with hyphen
rule.description: Two initials connected by a hyphen can mean “from–to,” in which case they should be written with a dash.
